        "content": "Spring AI is Spring’s project for building AI-powered applications with familiar Spring patterns. It gives you a consistent abstraction over different AI providers and models so you can integrate features like:

- chat/completions
- embeddings
- image generation
- audio/transcription
- vector stores
- retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- tool/function calling

The goal is to let you work with AI services in a Spring-friendly way, similar to how Spring abstracts databases or messaging systems.

### What it’s useful for
- Building chatbots and assistants
- Adding semantic search with embeddings + vector stores
- Creating RAG pipelines over your documents
- Connecting your app to multiple model providers with less code change
- Using Spring Boot auto-configuration and dependency injection patterns

### Typical architecture
Spring AI usually sits between your application and an AI provider:
- Your app calls Spring AI APIs
- Spring AI adapts that call to a provider like OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, etc.
- For retrieval use cases, Spring AI can connect to vector databases and document loaders

### Why people use it
- Familiar Spring conventions
- Provider-agnostic abstractions
- Easier testing and configuration
- Good fit for Spring Boot applications

### Official docs
- Spring AI reference documentation: https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/

If you want, I can also give you:

2. a comparison with LangChain,
